title: Yamagata — 山形
goal: Describe weather and connect a short explanation to an action.

blocks.text: Yamagata is both a prefecture and its capital city's name. Yamagata City's Kajo Park is associated with cherry blossoms; the wider prefecture also has mountain and snow scenery. Our weather sentences describe imaginary days, not the weather today.
**山形に行きました。** やまがたに いきました。 — I went to Yamagata.

We have already seen 山 in Matsushima. A city name now connects a familiar landscape shape with new weather vocabulary. We will distinguish “rain” as a noun from “cold” as an adjective instead of forcing all weather words into one inflection pattern.

items: **Character:** 山 · **Useful meaning/reading:** mountain; やま, サン · **Radical and visible parts:** 山, やま; whole mountain-derived form · **Role:** Formal review from Matsushima.

**Character:** 形 · **Useful meaning/reading:** shape/form; かた/かたち, ケイ/ギョウ; がた here · **Radical and visible parts:** 彡, さんづくり, beside an 开-shaped left section · **Role:** Encounter. Left shapes aid recognition; avoid reading the city by adding standalone words.

blocks.text: **山形 / やまがた**. The がた is the learned name reading; ordinary **形 / かたち**, shape, is only an assisted orientation word here. 彡 has three slanted strokes, unlike 川's river strokes or 三's horizontal number strokes. Identifying their arrangement is more useful than calling every three-stroke group “three.”

cards.title: 天 and 気 Make 天気

blocks.text: **天気 / てんき — weather.** 天 has radical **大**, だい; recognise the extra upper stroke in its whole shape. 気 has radical **气**, きがまえ, surrounding lower **メ**-like modern strokes. Those pieces do not make a literal “big cross” explanation of weather.
**天気がいいです。** てんきが いいです。 — The weather is good.
**天気が悪いです。** てんきが わるいです。 — The weather is bad.

悪い / わるい is assisted vocabulary, with 悪 not newly assigned formal study. Good/bad is a speaker's description. 天気 is a noun and does not itself change like an い-adjective. We learn the compound before wider 気 expressions.
**雨 / あめ — rain.** 雨 is its own radical, あめ; at the top of another character its form is called あめかんむり. The enclosed drops and upper line make a rain-related whole shape.
**今日は雨です。** きょうは あめです。 — It is rainy today / Today is rain.

今日 / きょう is reviewed as a whole time word from Hokkaido. A weather noun can be followed by です. We do not need the new verb “fall” to make a beginner weather sentence. **雨でした / あめでした**, it was rainy, uses the noun past introduced with prices in Akita.

**雪 / ゆき — snow; 白い雪 / しろいゆき — white snow.** Snow's indexing radical is **雨**, あめかんむり, above a lower **彐**-shaped section. That lower part is a recognition shape here, not a rule that snow means a hand.
**山に雪があります。** やまに ゆきが あります。 — There is snow on the mountain.
**雪は白いです。** ゆきは しろいです。 — Snow is white.
These two sentences use different predicates: existence あります and adjective description 白いです. The picture is invented. We are not claiming year-round snow at a particular Yamagata location.

cards.title: A Weather Noun Is Not an い-Adjective

items: **Meaning:** It is rain/rainy · **Japanese:** 雨です · **Reading:** あめです
**Meaning:** It was rain/rainy · **Japanese:** 雨でした · **Reading:** あめでした
**Meaning:** It is not rain/rainy · **Japanese:** 雨ではありません · **Reading:** あめではありません
**Meaning:** It was not rain/rainy · **Japanese:** 雨ではありませんでした · **Reading:** あめではありませんでした

blocks.text: This completes the four polite noun-description forms: です, ではありません, でした, ではありませんでした. The past negative keeps **ではありません** and adds **でした**. Do not construct **雨くない**: 雨 is a noun. It also differs from **雨がありません**, which states absence of rain rather than classifying the day's weather.

cards.title: Cold, Clear and Cloudy: Assisted Words

blocks.text: **寒い / さむい — cold, an い-adjective; 晴れ / はれ — clear/fair weather, noun; 曇り / くもり — cloudiness/cloudy weather, noun.** Their harder characters stay encounters here.
**今日は寒いです。** きょうは さむいです。 — It is cold today.
**昨日は寒かったです。** きのうは さむかったです。 — It was cold yesterday.
**今日は晴れです。** きょうは はれです。 — It is clear today.

昨日 / きのう is assisted time vocabulary. Its characters do not create another formal assignment. Use 寒かった for the adjective and 晴れでした for the noun; their English weather translations can look similar while Japanese grammar differs.

cards.title: ですから: A Reason and a Result

blocks.text: **ですから — so; therefore**, joining a preceding polite statement to a result.
**今日は雨です。ですから、店で休みます。** きょうは あめです。ですから、みせで やすみます。 — It is rainy today. So I rest at a shop.

The rain is given as the reason; resting at the shop is the narrator's choice. We are not making a universal claim about what people do in rain. Compare **でも**, contrast, and **そして**, addition/sequence. The word **から** inside ですから has a different function from **九時から**, from nine. Learn the connector in the whole pattern before broader reason-clause grammar.

cards.title: 気 Also Appears in 元気

blocks.text: **元気 / げんき — healthy; energetic**, a な-adjective word. 元 is assisted; 気 is now formal study.
**友だちは元気です。** ともだちは げんきです。 — My friend is well/energetic.

**元気な人 / げんきなひと — an energetic person.** Use な before a noun, unlike 寒い's adjective pattern. We do not equate health with a particular weather condition. **元気ではありません / げんきではありません**, not well/energetic, uses the familiar な-adjective negative. This shows how one character participates in different useful words without requiring every possible abstract sense of 気.
**昨日は雨でした。今日は晴れです。** きのうは あめでした。きょうは はれです。 — It was rainy yesterday. It is clear today.
**山に白い雪があります。でも、町には雪がありません。** やまに しろい ゆきが あります。でも、まちには ゆきが ありません。 — There is white snow on the mountain. But there is no snow in the town.

The second scene is fictional. には adds topic/contrast to the familiar location に; it does not turn a town into a person. Read snow's existence separately from the day's weather label. The connector shows a difference between two places.

items: Read 山形, 天気, 雨 and 雪. **Answer:** やまがた; てんき; あめ; ゆき.
What radical links 雪 with 電? **Answer:** 雨.
Make 雨です past negative. **Answer:** 雨ではありませんでした.
Make 寒いです past. **Answer:** 寒かったです.
What relationship does ですから introduce? **Answer:** the result/conclusion of the preceding reason.
Choose “an energetic person”: 元気な人 / 元気い人. **Answer:** 元気な人.

blocks.text: 山形 is やまがた. 天気 is weather; 雨 is rain; 雪 is snow. Rain/snow weather labels are nouns, while 寒い is an adjective. 雨でした differs from 寒かったです. 雨ではありませんでした is the noun past negative. ですから gives a reason-to-result link. 気 also appears in 元気.
**Recall task:** “It was rainy yesterday. It is clear today.” **Model:** 昨日は雨でした。今日は晴れです。 Keep unstudied characters assisted. Continue to Tsuruoka.
